title: Audit fleet: find Haven mimi-hubd/mimi-core defects, turn verified ones into vectors, replay against mimid (run as a Workflow)
description:
Mark, 2026-11-14 (IETF 127 table): run an agent fleet over havenmessenger/interop to find mistakes, unimplemented parts, glitches and edge conditions; turn them into vectors; run them against mimid too. Run it after the table, against a pinned Haven commit, since Haven is changing DIV-10 and other things during the hackathon. Mark starts it by asking for a workflow.

Plan (Workflow script, ~8 auditors plus one verifier per candidate):
1. Auditors, one per area, all against a pinned commit of havenmessenger/interop:
   - wire codecs: TLS-PL lengths, RFC 9420 varints, unknown enum values, trailing bytes, select and optional fields
   - each protocol-07 endpoint against the draft text and Haven's DIVERGENCES.md
   - hub state machine: consent, held leaves, epochs, replays, enforced bounds
   - room policy against room-policy-04
   - mimi-content-10
   - OpenMLS configuration: capabilities, GREASE, required components
   - trust boundary: mTLS, From checks, the JSON lane (it currently accepts KeyPackage publishes for other providers' users)
2. Every candidate must carry three things or be dropped: the exact draft section it breaks, quoted; a reproducing vector or request sequence; and that vector run against our own mimi-hubd built from the pinned commit (haven.reviewcommit.com or the run.sh namespace in tools/interop/haven/live).
3. A separate verifier per surviving candidate tries to disprove it from the code and draft only, not the auditor's argument.
4. Survivors become vectors in the same JSON shape as Haven's protocol07-vectors.json (new fixture directory with PROVENANCE), replayed through mimid's decoders and, where it applies, its hub, so the same edge cases test mimid. mimid failures become mimid beads.
5. Reporting: to Jason in Zulip #mimi or as comments on havenmessenger/interop#1, one finding at a time with Mark's OK. No new issues or PRs on havenmessenger repos.

Bar: the RustCrypto batch of April 2026 was rejected as LLM slop. Nothing goes upstream without a reproduction on a running hub and a quoted spec line.
